questions.q: EMR clusters in private subnets read terabytes from S3 every day through a NAT gateway, and NAT data processing dominates the network bill. What is the cheapest fix?

options.t: Add an S3 interface endpoint in each subnet
options.why: Wrong: it works, but interface endpoints cost per AZ-hour and per GB, so it is not the cheapest.

options.t: Add an S3 gateway endpoint and a route to it in the subnet route tables
options.why: Right: it is free and sends S3 traffic around the NAT gateway.

options.t: Replace the NAT gateway with a Transit Gateway
options.why: Wrong: TGW adds per-attachment and per-GB fees and gives no private path to S3.

options.t: Move the cluster to a public subnet
options.why: Wrong: this exposes the cluster and does not address the design requirement of private subnets.

questions.explain: Gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB are free and remove NAT data charges.
questions.remember: NAT cost caused by S3 or DynamoDB traffic from inside the VPC → gateway endpoint (free, route-table based).
variants: The same traffic comes from on-premises → S3 interface endpoint, because gateway endpoints are not reachable from on-prem.
The traffic goes to Kinesis or SQS → interface endpoint (gateway type exists only for S3 and DynamoDB).

questions.q: An on-premises ETL job must read S3 over Direct Connect without using the internet. A gateway endpoint already exists in the VPC. What should the team add?

options.t: A second S3 gateway endpoint in another subnet
options.why: Wrong: gateway endpoints are route entries inside the VPC and cannot be reached from on-premises.

options.t: An S3 interface endpoint (PrivateLink) reached over the private VIF
options.why: Right: interface endpoints are ENIs with private IPs that on-premises can reach over VPN or DX.

options.t: VPC peering to the on-premises network
options.why: Wrong: peering connects only VPCs, not on-premises networks.

options.t: An egress-only internet gateway
options.why: Wrong: it provides IPv6 outbound internet access, not private S3 access.

questions.explain: Hybrid access to S3 needs an interface endpoint; gateway endpoints are in-VPC only.
questions.remember: On-premises, peered VPC or TGW access to S3 privately → interface endpoint. In-VPC workloads → free gateway endpoint.
variants: Only workloads inside the same VPC and Region need S3 → gateway endpoint.
On-prem uses a public VIF instead → it can reach S3 public IPs without any endpoint.

questions.q: A custom NACL was added to a subnet and now clients connect but responses never return. Inbound rules allow port 443. What is the likely cause?

options.t: Security groups are stateless and block the reply
options.why: Wrong: security groups are stateful and allow return traffic automatically.

options.t: NACLs are stateless, so outbound ephemeral ports 1024-65535 must also be allowed
options.why: Right: the reply goes out on an ephemeral port and the NACL evaluates each direction separately.

options.t: The VPC local route was removed
options.why: Wrong: the local route always exists and cannot be removed.

options.t: The internet gateway is not attached
options.why: Wrong: an IGW is free and always attached to at most one VPC; it does not filter return traffic.

questions.explain: NACLs are stateless; you must allow both directions including ephemeral ports.
questions.remember: Return traffic fails after NACL changes → allow ephemeral ports 1024-65535, because NACLs are stateless; SGs are stateful.
variants: Need to block one IP range → NACL deny rule, since SGs only allow.
A custom NACL with no rules → denies all until rules are added; the default NACL allows all.

questions.q: A security team must block one malicious IP range from reaching every instance in a subnet. Which control does this?

options.t: A security group deny rule
options.why: Wrong: security groups have allow rules only.

options.t: A NACL deny rule with a low rule number
options.why: Right: NACLs support deny, apply at subnet level and use the first matching rule by number.

options.t: A route table entry to a NAT gateway
options.why: Wrong: routes do not filter by source for inbound traffic.

options.t: A VPC endpoint policy
options.why: Wrong: endpoint policies filter requests to AWS services, not internet sources.

questions.explain: Only NACLs can explicitly deny; rule order decides.
questions.remember: Explicit deny of an IP range → NACL (subnet level, ordered rules). Fine-grained least privilege → security groups.
variants: Allow DB access only from the app tier → security group referencing the app SG.
Need deep inspection or domain filtering → AWS Network Firewall.

questions.q: A Glue job attached to a VPC through a network connection fails because its worker ENIs cannot talk to each other. Which change is required?

options.t: Add a self-referencing inbound rule on the security group
options.why: Right: job ENIs share the SG and need to communicate with each other.

options.t: Attach an internet gateway to the VPC
options.why: Wrong: the ENIs would still need public IPs and it does not fix SG isolation.

options.t: Create a VPC peering connection to itself
options.why: Wrong: a VPC cannot peer with itself.

options.t: Replace the NACL with a security group
options.why: Wrong: both can exist; SGs do not replace NACLs.

questions.explain: Cluster-style services need a self-referencing security group rule.
questions.remember: Glue, EMR, Redshift, MWAA and MSK nodes talking to each other → security group with a self-referencing rule.
variants: The job also cannot reach S3 → add an S3 gateway endpoint or NAT.
Database access from the app tier → SG rule referencing the app SG.

questions.q: Security wants a bucket reachable only from the company VPC through its S3 gateway endpoint, and nothing else. Which design achieves it?

options.t: A bucket policy that denies requests when `aws:SourceVpce` is not that endpoint ID
options.why: Right: the Deny blocks every other network path.

options.t: An SG on the bucket allowing the VPC CIDR
options.why: Wrong: S3 buckets do not have security groups.

options.t: A NACL on the subnet allowing S3
options.why: Wrong: NACLs cannot restrict who reaches a bucket from elsewhere.

options.t: Peering the VPC to the S3 service VPC
options.why: Wrong: AWS services cannot be peered and S3 is not in a peerable VPC.

questions.explain: Use a bucket policy condition on the endpoint plus an endpoint policy.
questions.remember: Restrict a bucket to your network → bucket policy Deny unless `aws:SourceVpce` matches; use endpoint policies to limit which buckets the VPC can reach.
variants: Limit which buckets workloads in the VPC may reach → gateway endpoint policy with bucket ARNs.
Restrict by trusted identities → SCP or RCP in the data perimeter.

questions.q: A SaaS vendor and your company have overlapping CIDR ranges, but the vendor must call one internal API privately. What should you use?

options.t: VPC peering
options.why: Wrong: peering cannot route overlapping CIDRs.

options.t: Transit Gateway
options.why: Wrong: TGW also requires non-overlapping CIDRs.

options.t: PrivateLink: expose the API behind an NLB as an endpoint service
options.why: Right: it does not route networks, allows overlapping CIDRs and exposes only that service.

options.t: Site-to-Site VPN
options.why: Wrong: VPN also needs non-overlapping ranges.

questions.explain: PrivateLink exposes one service, one-way, without routing networks.
questions.remember: Overlapping CIDRs or exposing only one service → PrivateLink (NLB endpoint service). Few VPCs full access → peering; many VPCs plus on-prem → TGW.
variants: 30 VPCs plus on-prem must talk to each other → Transit Gateway.
Two VPCs, full access, no overlap → VPC peering.

questions.q: VPC A is peered with B, and B is peered with C. Instances in A cannot reach C. Routes and SGs for A-B and B-C are correct. Why?

options.t: Peering is not transitive; A and C need their own peering or a Transit Gateway
options.why: Right: peering never forwards traffic through B.

options.t: Peering supports only one connection per account
options.why: Wrong: a VPC can have many peerings.

options.t: The CIDRs must be advertised with BGP
options.why: Wrong: peering uses static route table entries, not BGP.

options.t: Security groups cannot be used across peering
options.why: Wrong: SG references work for same-Region peering, and this is not the issue.

questions.explain: No transitive routing over VPC peering.
questions.remember: A-B and B-C peering does not give A-C. Fix with a direct peering or Transit Gateway.
variants: Many VPCs are needed → Transit Gateway.
Peer's NAT or IGW needed through peering → not allowed (no edge-to-edge routing).

questions.q: A team must set up a link to on-premises this week for a data migration, with encryption. Direct Connect would take weeks. What fits?

options.t: Site-to-Site VPN
options.why: Right: it is IPsec-encrypted over the internet and ready in minutes.

options.t: Direct Connect dedicated 10 Gbps
options.why: Wrong: it needs weeks of provisioning for the cross-connect.

options.t: Client VPN
options.why: Wrong: it connects individual remote users, not a site.

options.t: VPC peering
options.why: Wrong: it connects VPCs, not on-premises networks.

questions.explain: VPN is the quick encrypted option; DX is slow to provision.
questions.remember: Fast link up in days → Site-to-Site VPN. Consistent high throughput → Direct Connect. DX is private but not encrypted by default.
variants: The VPN needs more than 1.25 Gbps → Transit Gateway with multiple tunnels and ECMP (BGP).
DX traffic must be encrypted → MACsec or IPsec VPN over DX.

questions.q: Auditors want evidence of which flows were accepted and rejected in a VPC, queried cheaply with SQL over months of data. What is the standard pattern?

options.t: VPC Flow Logs to S3 in Parquet, queried with Athena
options.why: Right: Flow Logs record accepted and rejected flows, and Parquet cuts Athena scan cost.

options.t: Traffic Mirroring to CloudWatch Logs
options.why: Wrong: mirroring copies packets to an appliance, which is heavier and costlier.

options.t: Reachability Analyzer on a schedule
options.why: Wrong: it analyses a configured path, not historical flows.

options.t: Route table association history
options.why: Wrong: it shows config, not traffic.

questions.explain: Flow Logs plus S3 plus Athena.
questions.remember: Who talks to whom, ACCEPT or REJECT, cost top talkers → VPC Flow Logs to S3 with Athena (they hold metadata, not payload).
variants: Need to know which component blocks one path right now → Reachability Analyzer.
Find unintended exposure paths → Network Access Analyzer.

questions.q: Pipeline jobs in a private subnet time out intermittently calling AWS APIs through a NAT gateway. Which CloudWatch metric confirms the likely cause?

options.t: `ErrorPortAllocation` greater than 0 on the NAT gateway
options.why: Right: it shows the NAT ran out of ports, which causes intermittent timeouts.

options.t: `TunnelState` of the VPN
options.why: Wrong: it concerns VPN tunnels, not NAT.

options.t: `ConnectionState` of Direct Connect
options.why: Wrong: it concerns a DX link, not NAT.

options.t: `PacketDropCountNoRoute` of the TGW
options.why: Wrong: it concerns Transit Gateway routing.

questions.explain: NAT port exhaustion shows as ErrorPortAllocation.
questions.remember: Intermittent timeouts through NAT → check ErrorPortAllocation; fix with interface or gateway endpoints and more NAT gateways.
variants: VPN tunnel down → TunnelState below 1.
Many small S3 or DynamoDB requests through NAT → move to gateway endpoints.

questions.q: A Lambda function in a VPC needs to call Kinesis and has no internet access since joining the VPC. What is the best fix with no public exposure?

options.t: Add a `kinesis-streams` interface endpoint (or a NAT gateway)
options.why: Right: this gives the VPC a private path to the API.

options.t: Add an S3 gateway endpoint
options.why: Wrong: gateway endpoints exist only for S3 and DynamoDB, so it does not help with Kinesis.

options.t: Assign an Elastic IP to the function
options.why: Wrong: Lambda ENIs cannot get public internet access this way.

options.t: Attach a second route table to the function
options.why: Wrong: routes alone do not give an internet or service path.

questions.explain: VPC-attached Lambdas need NAT or interface endpoints for AWS APIs.
questions.remember: VPC Lambda calling an AWS API → interface endpoint for that service (or NAT). S3 and DynamoDB → gateway endpoint.
variants: The function only reads S3 → S3 gateway endpoint is enough.
Endpoint exists but DNS resolves public IPs → enable private DNS, `enableDnsSupport` and `enableDnsHostnames`.
